fixture_name: Cloverleaf-to-urban interchange conversion — INT preliminary design (Wikimedia PD geometry)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: A retained shortened collector-distributor weave carrying a recorded 1,100 pcu/h design-year peak flow concentrates lane-change demand and is a well-established sideswipe/rear-end exposure mechanism, squarely relevant to raise at preliminary design before geometry is fixed.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim rests on recorded GA-drawing geometry and weave volume plus a verbatim EV-IN-015 quote that directly covers junction-type suitability for traffic volume, conflicting-stream treatment, and lane balance/through-lane continuity; EV-IN-004 corroborates stage-appropriate PIARC checklist applicability.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a PIARC advisory safety-concern verification at the preliminary-design stage with normative_basis_note null, keeping the safety question distinct from any compliance assertion and respecting the international-baseline semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and staged: run the cited junction prompts, evaluate weaving adequacy with HSM Part C interchange models or IHSDM, then lengthen the weave or meter the entry if inadequate — concrete, contingent, and feasible at preliminary design.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRU exposure is explicitly addressed and reasonably scoped out because the shared-use paths are grade-separated from the motorised weave, satisfying the acknowledge-when-not-applicable case.

justifications.substance: Uncontrolled free-flow ramp-terminal crossings conflicting with retained shared-use paths is a genuine, well-targeted preliminary-design safety issue squarely aligned with the scheme's stated VRU continuity objectives.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim (pedestrian/cyclist provision required at junctions) is backed by a verbatim PIARC Appendix 1 quote (EV-IN-016) plus corroborating EV-IN-005, and the scheme-side facts (objectives, retained paths, loop ramps) are stated as recorded inputs; only the 'northern' loop label slightly exceeds the cited text without undermining the pivot.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern under the PIARC-derived international baseline, using checklist prompts as supporting basis rather than asserting non-compliance, keeping the safety question categorically distinct from any compliance determination.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: names concrete treatments (signalised or grade-separated crossings) at identified locations (both retained loop-ramp terminals, northern path crossing) and applicable tools (Walkability Checklist, CQSI), all viable at preliminary-design stage.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are the explicit focus of the finding, with their exposure at each ramp-terminal/path interface directly analysed and carried through to the recommendation.
